formulations.label: Prolonged-release tablets
formulations.note: Clinic product: 30 mg 'retard' tablet. No UK 30 mg retard (twice-daily) nifedipine tablet SmPC was found on emc or MHRA products. This entry uses the UK once-daily 30 mg prolonged-release tablet SmPC. Its doses, and its contraindications tied to that formulation (hepatic impairment, GI narrowing, Kock pouch, inflammatory bowel disease), belong to the once-daily product. UK twice-daily retard nifedipine tablets (20 mg) are dosed every 12 hours, so confirm the release type of the clinic product before using the doses here.

src.q: Each prolonged-release tablet contains 30 mg nifedipine.
Owing to the duration of action of the formulation, Adalat LA should not be administered to patients with hepatic impairment.
The recommended dose is one tablet (20 mg) every 12 hours.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: All grades of hypertension; prophylaxis of chronic stable angina (alone or with a beta-blocker).

src.q: For the treatment of all grades of hypertension. For the prophylaxis of chronic stable angina pectoris either as monotherapy or in combination with a beta-blocker.

items.t: Not for acute angina attacks, not for secondary prevention of MI; safety in malignant hypertension not established.

src.q: should not be used for the treatment of acute attacks of angina.
should not be used for secondary prevention of myocardial infarction.
The safety of Adalat LA in malignant hypertension has not been established.

items.t: Hypertension: mild to moderate start 20 mg once daily; severe start 30 mg once daily; up to a maximum of 90 mg once daily.

src.q: In mild to moderate hypertension, the recommended initial dose is one 20 mg tablet once-daily. In severe hypertension, the recommended initial dose is one 30 mg tablet once-daily.
up to a maximum of 90 mg once-daily.

items.t: Angina prophylaxis: start 30 mg once daily; up to a maximum of 90 mg once daily. When switching from another calcium-channel blocker, start at 30 mg once daily.

src.q: For the prophylaxis of angina pectoris, the recommended initial dose is one 30 mg tablet once-daily.
Patients switched from other calcium antagonists should initiate therapy at the recommended initial dose of 30 mg Adalat LA once-daily.

items.t: Different UK product (twice-daily retard 20 mg tablets): 20 mg every 12 hours, up to 40 mg every 12 hours. Shown only because the clinic product is labelled retard; the once-daily doses above do not apply to a twice-daily retard tablet.

src.q: The recommended dose is one tablet (20 mg) every 12 hours.
The dosage may be increased up to 40 mg every 12 hours to achieve the desired effect.

items.t: Elderly over 65 years and renal impairment: no dose adjustment needed.

src.q: Based on pharmacokinetic data for Adalat LA no dose adaptation in elderly people above 65 years is necessary.
no dosage adjustment is required in patients with renal impairment

items.t: Safety and efficacy below 18 years not established.

src.q: The safety and efficacy of Adalat LA in children below 18 years has not been established.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to nifedipine, other dihydropyridines (theoretical cross-reactivity) or excipients.

src.q: should not be administered to patients with known hypersensitivity to the active substance, or to other dihydropyridines because of the theoretical risk of cross-reactivity

items.t: Cardiogenic shock; clinically significant aortic stenosis; unstable angina; during or within one month of a myocardial infarction.

src.q: Adalat LA should not be used in cases of cardiogenic shock, clinically significant aortic stenosis, unstable angina, or during or within one month of a myocardial infarction.

items.t: Hepatic impairment (long duration of action of this formulation).

src.q: Owing to the duration of action of the formulation, Adalat LA should not be administered to patients with hepatic impairment.

items.t: History of gastrointestinal or oesophageal obstruction or any narrowing of the GI tract; Kock pouch; inflammatory bowel disease or Crohn's disease.

src.q: should not be administered to patients with a history of gastro-intestinal obstruction, oesophageal obstruction, or any degree of decreased lumen diameter of the gastro-intestinal tract.
Adalat LA must not be used in patients with a Kock pouch (ileostomy after proctocolectomy).
Adalat LA is contra-indicated in patients with inflammatory bowel disease or Crohn's disease.

items.t: With rifampicin (nifedipine levels too low).

src.q: Adalat LA should not be administered concomitantly with rifampicin since effective plasma levels of nifedipine may not be achieved owing to enzyme induction

items.t: Hypotension: caution; care if systolic BP below 90 mmHg.

src.q: Caution should be exercised in patients with hypotension as there is a risk of further reduction in blood pressure and care must be exercised in patients with very low blood pressure (severe hypotension with systolic blood pressure less than 90 mm Hg).

items.t: Poor cardiac reserve: use with caution; heart failure has occasionally worsened.

src.q: Adalat LA should be used with caution in patients whose cardiac reserve is poor. Deterioration of heart failure has occasionally been observed with nifedipine.

items.t: Non-digestible tablet shell: may appear in stools; obstructive symptoms and, very rarely, bezoars can occur.

src.q: Bezoars can occur in very rare cases and may require surgical intervention.

items.t: Diabetes: control may need adjusting. Dialysis with malignant hypertension and hypovolaemia: marked fall in blood pressure possible.

src.q: Diabetic patients taking Adalat LA may require adjustment of their control.
In dialysis patients with malignant hypertension and hypovolaemia, a marked decrease in blood pressure can occur.

items.t: With beta-blockers or other antihypertensives: additive effect may cause postural hypotension. Does not prevent rebound after stopping other antihypertensives.

src.q: the possibility of an additive effect resulting in postural hypotension should be borne in mind.
Adalat LA will not prevent possible rebound effects after cessation of other antihypertensive therapy.

items.t: CYP3A4 inhibitors (macrolides e.g. erythromycin, azole antifungals e.g. ketoconazole, HIV protease inhibitors, fluoxetine, nefazodone, valproic acid, cimetidine, diltiazem): raise nifedipine levels; monitor blood pressure and consider a lower nifedipine dose.

src.q: Drugs increasing nifedipine exposure: - macrolide antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin) - anti-HIV protease inhibitors (e.g., ritonavir) - azole anti-mycotics (e.g., ketoconazole) - fluoxetine
valproic acid - cimetidine - diltiazem
Upon co-administration of known inhibitors of the cytochrome P450 3A4 system, the blood pressure should be monitored and, if necessary, a reduction in the nifedipine dose considered

items.t: CYP3A4 inducers (rifampicin - contraindicated; phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital): lower nifedipine levels; monitor response and consider a dose increase (and reduce again when the inducer stops).

src.q: Drugs decreasing nifedipine exposure: - rifampicin (see above) - phenytoin - carbamazepine - phenobarbital
Upon co-administration of inducers of the cytochrome P450 3A4 system, the clinical response to nifedipine should be monitored and, if necessary, an increase in the nifedipine dose considered.

items.t: Beta-blockers: monitor carefully (heart failure may worsen in isolated cases). Other antihypertensives: increased blood pressure lowering.

src.q: When nifedipine is administered simultaneously with ß-receptor blockers the patient should be carefully monitored, since deterioration of heart failure is also known to develop in isolated cases.
Nifedipine may increase the blood pressure lowering effect of concomitant applied antihypertensives.

items.t: Grapefruit or grapefruit juice: avoid (raised levels, effect may last 3 days).

src.q: Ingestion of grapefruit/grapefruit juice is therefore to be avoided while taking nifedipine

items.t: Digoxin (check for digoxin toxicity), quinidine (monitor levels), tacrolimus (monitor levels, consider lower dose). IV magnesium sulfate in pregnancy: monitor blood pressure carefully.

src.q: The patient should therefore be subjected to precautionary checks for symptoms of digoxin overdosage
Careful monitoring of blood pressure must be exercised when administering nifedipine with I.V. magnesium sulfate

items.t: No dose adjustment needed in renal impairment.

src.q: Based on pharmacokinetic data, no dosage adjustment is required in patients with renal impairment

items.t: Prolonged-release tablets should not be given in hepatic impairment (4.3). Section 4.4 also says impaired liver function needs careful monitoring and, in severe cases, possibly a dose reduction.

src.q: Owing to the duration of action of the formulation, Adalat LA should not be administered to patients with hepatic impairment.
In patients with impaired liver function careful monitoring and, in severe cases, a dose reduction may be necessary.

items.t: SmPC: should not be used in pregnancy unless the woman needs nifedipine; reserve for severe hypertension unresponsive to standard therapy; very careful individual risk-benefit assessment.

src.q: Adalat LA should not be used during pregnancy unless the clinical condition of the woman requires treatment with nifedipine.
Adalat LA should be reserved for women with severe hypertension who are unresponsive to standard therapy
any use in pregnancy requires a very careful individual risk benefit assessment

items.t: BUMPS (calcium-channel blockers): nifedipine is commonly used in pregnancy and unlikely to cause harm; no extra monitoring for major birth defects.

src.q: Nifedipine is commonly used in pregnancy and is unlikely to cause harm.
No extra monitoring for major birth defects is required following use of a calcium channel blocker.

items.t: SmPC: excreted in milk in small amounts; no specific safety concerns from limited data; advise watching for low blood pressure in the infant; weigh benefit of breastfeeding against benefit of therapy.

src.q: Limited clinical evidence suggests no specific safety concerns, but patients should be advised of signs of low blood pressure in the infant
Decisions on whether to breastfeed during treatment or to abstain from nifedipine therapy should take into account the benefit of breastfeeding for the child and the benefit of therapy for the woman.

items.t: SPS: the dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker of choice (very small amounts in milk); as a precaution monitor the infant for hypotension. Applies to any formulation, including modified-release.

src.q: This is a preferred choice due to very small amounts in breast milk and extensive experience of use during breastfeeding.
Recommendations apply to any indication the medicine is being used for and to any formulation, including modified-release preparations.

items.t: Male fertility: reversible sperm changes reported in IVF; consider nifedipine as a cause in men with repeated unsuccessful IVF.

src.q: calcium antagonists like nifedipine should be considered as possible causes.

items.t: Common: oedema (9.9%, including peripheral oedema), headache (3.9%), vasodilatation, constipation, feeling unwell (others below 3%).

src.q: ADRs listed under "common" were observed with a frequency below 3% with the exception of oedema (9.9%) and headache (3.9%).
Oedema (incl. peripheral oedema) Vasodilatation

items.t: Allergic oedema/angioedema including larynx oedema (may be life-threatening); anaphylactic reactions; agranulocytosis; toxic epidermal necrolysis; jaundice; bezoar and intestinal obstruction.

src.q: Allergic oedema/angioedema (incl. larynx oedema*)
* = may result in life-threatening outcome
Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis

items.t: Chest pain (angina) may occur. Pulmonary oedema reported when used as a tocolytic in pregnancy.

src.q: Chest pain (Angina pectoris)
**cases have been reported when used as tocolytic during pregnancy

items.t: Overdose: reduced consciousness to coma, hypotension, tachy- or bradycardia, hyperglycaemia, metabolic acidosis, cardiogenic shock with pulmonary oedema; observe at least 12 hours after a sustained-release overdose.

src.q: Disturbances of consciousness to the point of coma, a drop in blood pressure, tachycardia, bradycardia, hyperglycaemia, metabolic acidosis, hypoxia, cardiogenic shock with pulmonary oedema.
for 12 hours if a sustained release preparation has been taken.

items.t: Swallow whole with water, with or without food; never bite, chew or break. Take at about the same time each day, preferably in the morning.

src.q: The tablets should be swallowed whole with a glass of water, either with or without food.
under no circumstances should they be bitten, chewed or broken up.
The tablets should be taken at approximately 24-hour intervals, i.e. at the same time each day, preferably during the morning.

items.t: The empty tablet shell may be seen in the stools; this is expected.

src.q: As the outer membrane of the Adalat LA tablet is not digested, what appears to be the complete tablet may be seen in the toilet or associated with the patient's stools.

items.t: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.

src.q: Ingestion of grapefruit/grapefruit juice is therefore to be avoided while taking nifedipine

items.t: Driving may be affected, especially at the start, on changes, or with alcohol.

src.q: This applies particularly at the start of treatment, on changing the medication and in combination with alcohol.
